label: M-05
title: Annihilation and ordinary phUSD minting share one daily budget, and the annihilation path extracts 2x per unit of budget - griefing the on-ramp is the most profitable use of it
fingerprintNote: sha256(contract:function:rootCauseClass)[:16] - legacy form, empty entryPoint. Carried verbatim from sanitized.json; reproduces from fingerprintBasis.

classification.assetImpact: Availability, not assets. The protocol's ordinary permissionless stablecoin->phUSD on-ramp is deniable for a given stablecoin for the remainder of a 24h window, by an actor who is PAID for doing it: an ordinary minter gets 1 phUSD per unit of shared budget, an annihilator gets 2. The DoS costs nothing because it is a side effect of a profitable trade. Window-reset semantics (restart on the first mint after expiry, not a fixed schedule) additionally hand the annihilator control over when each window opens.
attackPath: 1. Annihilator holds antimatter and the registered stablecoin.
2. Calls annihilateFrom sized to consume the remaining config.mintedToday budget at :227 - the identical counter the general on-ramp charges.
3. Ordinary depositors are refused ('Daily mint limit exceeded') for the rest of the window while the annihilator has extracted 2x per unit of budget consumed.
4. By timing the first mint after expiry, the annihilator also chooses when the next window starts.
classification.likelihood: Medium-high once antimatter is emitted - the griefing is not an extra cost, it is the most profitable way to use the budget, so a rational annihilator does it by default.
classification.assumptions: maxMintPerDay is set non-zero for the stablecoin; the annihilator holds enough antimatter to consume the window's budget.
classification.externalRequirements: Live antimatter emission (same PARK-003 caveat as M-02) and a non-zero cap.

justification: C4 Medium on the availability limb: 'the function of the protocol or its availability could be impacted'. The external requirements are real and stated (emission must be live, cap non-zero), which is exactly what Medium permits and what keeps it off High - there is no theft, the condition self-resolves each window, and no user loses funds. Not Low, because denying the protocol's general on-ramp at zero marginal cost to a party the protocol is simultaneously paying is a structural incentive defect, not an incidental one. Confidence is medium and is recorded as such. Deliberately NOT collapsed with M-03: same counter, different root cause (under-counting vs profitable budget exhaustion), different impact class, different mitigation - collapsing would bury the DoS.
recommendation: Give the annihilation path its own budget, or charge the antimatter leg too (which also fixes DEDUP-002) so the two paths consume budget proportionally to what they issue.
Use a fixed epoch boundary to remove the first-minter timing control.

sanitizer.reason: No known-issues document exists for this project (knownIssuesFile/Source null, knownIssues empty, verified at HEAD) so KI suppression has no authority; no C4 known-invalid class genuinely applies; not a malicious-owner vector; ledger empty so no prior entry to reconcile against.

additionalContext.rootCause: PhusdStableMinter.mint is the protocol's general permissionless phUSD on-ramp; Antimatter routes through the identical function and charges the same config.mintedToday. An ordinary minter gets 1 phUSD per unit of budget; an annihilator gets 2.
additionalContext.impact: Denial of the protocol's ordinary stablecoin->phUSD on-ramp for a given stablecoin for the remainder of a 24h window, achieved by a party who is PAID ~$1 per unit for doing it. Cost of the DoS is zero - it is a side effect of a profitable trade. The window-reset semantics (restart on the first mint after expiry, not on a fixed schedule) additionally let the annihilator control when each window opens.
affectedParties: any downstream protocol path that mints phUSD through PhusdStableMinter
additionalContext.assumptionGap: Bites only when maxMintPerDay is non-zero; registerStablecoin defaults it to 0 = unlimited. If the operator never sets a cap, DEDUP-006 is inert and DEDUP-002 is moot - but then there is no issuance rate limit at all, which is DEDUP-004.
additionalContext.severityRationale: C4 Medium: protocol function/availability impacted. Not High: no theft, self-resolving each window, and only bites when maxMintPerDay is set non-zero.

mergeAction: KEPT SEPARATE from DEDUP-002. Verified before deciding: both concern PhusdStableMinter's maxMintPerDay counter, but the root causes differ - DEDUP-002 is 'the counter under-counts issuance by 2x', DEDUP-006 is 'the counter is a shared budget an annihilator can profitably exhaust'. Different impact class (availability/DoS vs mis-sized rail), different mitigation (separate budget per path + fixed epoch boundary vs charging the AM leg). Collapsing them would bury the DoS.
